questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

My pocket has been picked.

options.text: Someone’s pocket has been picked by me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Someone has picked my pocket."** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **subject** of the provided sentence is clearly being "**acted upon**" (or is in the** passive form**), so, we have to **apply verbs** **according** to the **passive **voice.
 
• Apparently, the sentence is in **present perfect tense** form as the event that is being talked about has already started in the past and is having an effect on the present **(has + been)**, so we will use the following structure:
 
• Active Voice : **Subject + has/have+ v3+ object**
 
• Passive Voice: **Object+ has/have+ been+ V3+ by + subject**
 
 
• Example: *Nikita has challenged Leena. (**Active**)*
 
• Example:* Leena has been challenged by Nikita. (**Passive**)*
 
 
 
• Thus, the active voice of "My pocket has been **picked**" is "Someone **has** picked my pocket".
 
• Hence, the active voice is: *Someone has picked my pocket.​*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Let us take a look at the remaining sentences:

 
• Someone’s pocket has been picked by me - This is **not **an **active voice** form as (**by**) is applied here.
 
• Someone had my pocket picked - This is in the **past perfect tense** **(had**) and we require present perfect tense (has) so this sentence is also **incorrect**.
 
• I picked someone’s pocket - This sentence is in the **simple past tense** (**picked**) and we need present perfect tense (has) so this sentence is also **not** **appropriate**.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"the fastest"**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined segment does need to be substituted.
 
• A superlative adjective conveys an **attribute's** extreme or** maximum degree**. To convey the exceptional quality of one thing among a group of things, we employ a superlative adjective (**not two things**).
 
• Evidently, a **race** is a **competition **between more than two people. Thus, we will use a** superlative degree** of comparison.
 
 
• Example: *The lady in the main office is the smartest employee in this department.*
 
 
 
• Furthermore, the adjective's **superlative** form is followed by the article **"the."**
 
• That is why **"the fastest" **is **appropriate** to apply in the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the substituted sentence is: *She should run the fastest to win the race.​*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Positive, comparative, and superlative degrees of comparison are the **three** **categories** for degrees of comparison.
 
• The degree of comparison of "**fast**" is:
 
• **Positive** degree: **Fast**
 
• **Comparative **degree: **Faster**
 
• **Superlative** degree: **Fastest**

questions.question:
Identify the option that arranges the given parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

a) PB Shelly was an English poet.

b) He was expelled from Oxford for publishing a tract entitled ‘The Necessity of Atheism’.

c) He detested tyranny and institutionalised servitude.

d) Born into a wealthy upper-class family
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**a, d, c, b**" [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given **stanza** is talking **about** an English **poet **named **PB Shelly** so, the **first sentence** must be the** introductory** sentence of that poet.
 
• **Sentence a**, that is, ' PB Shelly was an English poet' is **introducing** the main **subject** of this paragraph. Thus, it is the first sentence.
 
• **Sentence d**, that is, 'Born into a wealthy upper-class family' is **mentioning** the** birth** and circumstances of the** poet**. So, this will be the second sentence.
 
• **Sentence c**, that is, 'He detested tyranny and institutionalized servitude' is **continuing** the **story** of PB Shelly and telling us how he hated tyranny. That is why this will be the third sentence.
 
• **Sentence b**, that is, 'He was expelled from Oxford for publishing a tract entitled "The Necessity of Atheism"' is the **conclusive** sentence and the **remaining **one. Thus, this will be the last sentence.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is: *a, d, c, b​*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• As can be seen, the question given above concerns **para jumbles**. It describes a **paragraph** in which the **sentences** are **mixed up** and each is assigned a letter or number as a label.
 
• The following are some easy methods for resolving ParaJumbles:
 
• **Determine** the passage's **aim**.
 
• **Find** the **keywords** and indicators.
 
• **Use** nouns, pronouns, and **antecedents** to your advantage.

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

The movie I watched last Saturday was __much better interesting__ than the one I watched today.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**much more interesting**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This sentence needs improvement.
 
• We can't say "more better" because "**better**" is the **comparative** version of "**good**". So we may now say "**much better**." In order to convey that something is **desirable**, we can say "much better."
 
• Additionally, "**much**" is used to** describe** a lot or a** bunch** of anything. The** comparative** degree of "**much** or many" is the word "**more**." It denotes "a larger quantity" of something.
 
• In the above-mentioned sentence, "**movie**" is the **noun** and "**interesting**" is **modifying** "**movie**". So, if we will put "better" with "interesting" then the sentence will become **redundant **and ultimately incorrect.
 
• Thus, we will apply "**much more interesting**" in the sentence to improve it.
 
• The complete sentence is: *The movie I watched last Saturday was much more interesting__ than the one I watched today.**​*​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The **degrees of comparison** refer to how an **adjective **alters its form to **demonstrate comparison**.
 
• **Positive**, **comparative**, and **superlative **degrees of comparison are the several categories for degrees of comparison.
 
• The **superlative** form of "**many/much**" is "**most**," while the **comparative **form is **"more**."
